scenes.heading: Host–pathogen relationships
scenes.sub: An evolutionary contest that never ends
scenes.say: Every pathogen needs hosts to survive and spread, and every host fights back. In Australia you can see this contest play out, from rabbits and myxoma virus to Tasmanian devils.

scenes.heading: Kinds of pathogen
scenes.say: Infection is the guest arriving. Disease is the guest wrecking the house. Pathogens range from prions and viruses, which aren't cells, to bacteria, fungi, protists and parasitic animals. Antibiotics need a bacterial target, like a cell wall, so they do nothing to viruses.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A meme goes viral if each person shares it with more than one other
scenes.science: An outbreak grows if R₀ is greater than 1
scenes.breaks: Real infections don't spread evenly, and R₀ assumes everyone is susceptible, so spread changes as people become immune.
scenes.say: Think of a meme. If each person shares it with more than one new person, it goes viral. Fewer than one, it fizzles. That average is R nought. If enough people mute their chats, the meme stops: that's herd immunity.
scenes.caption: Think of a meme. If each person shares it with more than one new person, it goes viral. Fewer than one, it fizzles. That average is R₀. If enough people mute their chats, the meme stops: that's herd immunity.

scenes.heading: Herd immunity threshold
scenes.say: R nought above one spreads, below one fades. The fraction of people who must be immune is about one minus one over R nought.
scenes.caption: R₀ above 1 spreads, below 1 fades. The fraction of people who must be immune is about 1 − 1/R₀.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Measles has R₀ = 15. What fraction of people must be immune?
scenes.say: Measles has an R nought of about fifteen. One minus one fifteenth is zero point nine three three. So about ninety-three percent of people must be immune. That's why even a small drop in vaccination can let outbreaks start.
scenes.caption: Measles has an R₀ of about 15. 1 − 1/15 = 0.933. So about 93% of people must be immune. That's why even a small drop in vaccination can let outbreaks start.

scenes.heading: Exo vs endo
scenes.say: Toxins are one kind of virulence factor. Exo means exits: exotoxins are proteins bacteria secrete, like tetanus and cholera toxins. Endo means embedded: endotoxins are part of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, released when the cells die.

scenes.heading: Myxoma and rabbits
scenes.say: When myxoma virus was released in 1950, it killed most infected rabbits. But strains that killed too fast gave mosquitoes too little time to pick them up, and mild strains were cleared too soon. Intermediate strains spread best, while rabbits evolved resistance. It's a trade-off, not a march to harmlessness.

Quick recap. Infection isn't the same as disease. Antibiotics don't work on viruses. R nought above one spreads. Herd immunity is about one minus one over R nought. And hosts and pathogens coevolve in an arms race. Now try the practice questions!
